announcements.title: v2.8.5: New Feedback & Feature Requests page in the plugin; four unsupported models discontinued
announcements.html:
The plugin settings page now has a “Feedback & Feature Requests” section—the 14th tab, sharing the same entry point as the standalone console. After signing in with GitHub, you can report issues or suggest features; submissions automatically include your version and platform for easier diagnosis. Login only requests your public identity and no repository permissions; the token stays on your machine and is inaccessible to the page, so even if the page is injected with a script, credentials cannot be stolen.

Four models have been removed from the EAC channel: opencode/flint-40b-free, opencode/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free, opencode/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-free, and mimo-v2.6-flash-free. They were previously only available through the OpenCode residential lane, which has been decommissioned; the EAC page model count drops from 19 to 16. The two 400K models tagged high-speed and blast are unaffected—they are served by Dahl Inference and remain operational (0% errors in the past hour, ~20ms latency).

The model plaza (new-api) has been updated accordingly: these four models no longer appear as cards; the plaza now counts Dahl consumption in its statistics, which previously showed 0 because pricing was set to 0. The two 400K models have also been given descriptions and tags in the plaza.

Simultaneously released on npm as @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.8.5; the bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm remains a third-party repackaging—do not install it.

announcements.title: v2.8.4: Documentation for the two 400K high-speed EAC models; magpie engine label added to Model Workbench
announcements.html:
2.8.4 documented the upstream data processing terms for the two 400K high-speed EAC models (see the other pinned notice on this page), and added engine annotations to the Model Workbench—it is now called Model Workbench (magpie), matching the built-in descriptor in the extension marketplace.

Several fixes were also merged: the two Dahl models on the EAC channel had their context calibrated to 400K and output cap set to 8192, with vision marked as unsupported per actual upstream capability; AMD Radeon gained capability tables for nine models; the card performance capsule now reads real-time data from this site's /api/perf-metrics (the two Dahl models don't show capsules yet because their 24-hour window spans a channel switch and data is still stabilizing—they will appear automatically after a full window). Feedback entry issues were fixed: the default feedback address was missing the /feedback prefix, causing login and submission to 404; the token-expired state no longer perpetually shows “logged in”; 26 vendor icons were invisible in dark theme due to missing fill; spotlight and tilt highlights were overlapping. Simultaneously released on npm as @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.8.4; the bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm remains a third-party repackaging—do not install it.

announcements.title: Important Notice: Upstream Data Processing for the Two 400K High-Speed EAC Models
announcements.html:
The two 400K-context models marked high-speed and blast in the EAC cooperative channel (DeepSeek V4 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash) are served by the upstream provider Dahl Inference. Before using them, please read the following four points. These are statements made by the upstream provider, not assessments by this plugin:

  • Requests may be processed by independent compute operators across a distributed network, rather than through an isolated network within a single data center.
  • The upstream provider does not guarantee zero data retention or end-to-end confidentiality for its standard service.
  • Compute operators may have access to request contents while processing requests.
  • Some completed API requests may, after anonymization, be used for load and reliability testing in test environments.

Therefore: Do not send passwords, API keys, personal identification information, business secrets, or anything you do not want third parties to process to these two models. For sensitive content, use your own paid API through an aggregation provider or choose another model. The plugin itself does not upload anything—usage data, settings, and forwarding keys remain on your local machine. However, prompts and tool results sent to a model necessarily pass through the upstream provider.

Issue Reports & Feature Requests: You can submit them through the “Feedback & Feature Requests” tab in the plugin settings, or through “Project Support → Feedback & Feature Requests” in the standalone console's left sidebar. Sign in with GitHub to submit. Report any OFM issues or suggest features you would like to see. Your version and platform information are automatically included to help diagnose problems.

Additionally, we are experimenting with building a fully automated workflow for maintaining open-source projects based on EACbot (issue classification, reproduction, regression testing, and release checks). EACbot is currently experimental and under development; it is not yet stable and does not accept official issue reports. Please continue using the feedback channels above rather than submitting issues directly through EACbot.

announcements.title: v2.8.3: Fixed Claude subscription TUI interaction mode getting stuck for 45 seconds before falling back to -p
announcements.html:
Version 2.8.3 permanently fixes the issue where Claude subscription users could not use TUI interactive mode with the magpie engine and had to wait 45 seconds before falling back to -p. Starting with Claude Code 2.1.316+, the first run displays an additional security notice (press Enter to continue) and terminal configuration screen (press Esc to skip). The old engine did not recognize these screens: Claude waited for keypresses while the engine waited for a prompt. Both sides waited until the 45-second timeout, then abandoned TUI mode and fell back to -p. Repeated failures also triggered a backoff period of up to 24 hours. This was the root cause of the TUI issue.

The engine has now incorporated the upstream fix (eef99e4). Both onboarding screens are automatically acknowledged, restoring TUI mode. Subscription usage is charged through the interactive CLI entry point, which costs nearly half as much as the -p SDK CLI.

The release manifest also temporarily exceeded the 80-file limit after the new engine update, reaching 81 files and causing older updaters to reject installation. Zopfli compression brought it back within the 80-file budget while retaining standard gzip compatibility and unchanged verification logic. Also released on npm as @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.8.3; the bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm remains a third-party repackaging—do not install it.

announcements.title: A Personal Request: Please Consider Giving These Three Projects a GitHub Star
announcements.html:
This plugin is free, ad-free, and does not require you to sign in to any account. Writing and maintaining it, and getting up in the middle of the night to fix compatibility whenever upstream releases a new version, all depend on the enthusiasm of the same group of people. For open-source projects, the only reward is those little GitHub Stars—they largely determine how many more nights the developers can afford to invest.

If you have used this plugin and found that it saved you money or time, please take thirty seconds to look at these three projects by the same author. If one is useful to you, consider giving it a Star. If none is relevant, that's perfectly fine. Simply taking the time to read this means a lot to the developer.

  • EAC-Desktop — An open-source desktop workspace based on DeepSeek Harness, featuring native Tauri windows, a bundled Node.js runtime, and an integrated environment for projects, sessions, plugins, and themes.
  • EAC-Pack — An integrated plugin suite that brings hundreds of DSH plugins together and allows them to coexist seamlessly.
  • EAC-design-world — A local video production and design environment featuring multitrack editing, templates and design systems, a native preview canvas, and real file exports, without handing your assets to anyone else.

All three repositories are actively maintained. A GitHub Star costs nothing, but means a great deal to the developer. Thank you to everyone who made it this far.

announcements.title: v2.8.2: Automatic Extension Marketplace Updates with a Security Observation Window, Migration Manifest, and Model Marketplace
announcements.html:
Version 2.8.2 addresses two missing capabilities in the extension marketplace: automatic updates and migration. Automatic updates are disabled by default. When enabled, the marketplace periodically refreshes its index and automatically installs updates for extensions that are enabled and have passed the observation window. A new version must remain available for at least two hours from the first time it is detected locally before it can be installed automatically (following the supply-chain observation window introduced by VS Code in 2026). Manual updates remain available during this period. Disabled extensions will never be automatically enabled. The Installed page now displays the latest release note and observation-window countdown directly on each extension card.

The migration assistant is also available: the Installed page can export the current extension manifest (IDs, versions, enabled/disabled status, and configuration) as JSON. After moving to another machine or reinstalling, you can reinstall the extensions and restore their configurations with one click. Secrets are never exported. Extension detail dialogs now include a model marketplace showing which models a channel plugin provides before installation. The page header adds an index-source badge (live mirror or built-in snapshot) and an automatic-update toggle. The bottom of the Installed page now displays a recent activity log covering installation, enable/disable actions, configuration changes, and automatic updates.

The desktop extension center also receives all these capabilities, along with a fix for incorrectly reporting an available update after a version rollback. Official extension covers and release notes have been published in the marketplace repository. Also released on npm as @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.8.2; the bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm remains a third-party repackaging—do not install it.

announcements.title: v2.8.0: Free Lane Request-Shaping Layer Aligned with Reference Gateway v1.4.6; One-Command Engine Updates
announcements.html:
Version 2.8.0 replaces the anonymous free-lane request-shaping layer with a file-by-file port of the reference gateway opencode2api v1.4.6. All client tools are renamed to opaque aliases before being sent upstream, so external client tool names are never exposed. The 13 official 2.1 CLI tool definitions and the complete official system prompts have been added. Each request receives a fresh 40-hex project ID, preventing quota from being concentrated in the shared global bucket. Endpoints have been changed to the 2.1 client-family paths, and session ID generation now uses a slow clock to ensure dates always fall within the upstream acceptance window. These changes address the three categories of access gates behind the recurring 429 errors that occurred even when request formats appeared correct.

The bundled Magpie engine has been updated to upstream commit 6a900e0d from 2026-10-31. Builds now use the same trimming flags as upstream releases, reducing the gzip payload from 45.3 MB to 27.2 MB. The release package now contains 77 files, safely below the older updater's 80-file limit. A new update:magpie command makes future engine updates a one-command operation with automatic rollback on failure. This release also fixes a numeric input being partially clipped in a narrow settings panel. A new npm test prevents publishing a stale bundle: source changes without rebuilding the release bundle will now cause the test to fail.

This release updates the plugin package only. The desktop application version and installers are unchanged. Also released on npm as @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.8.0; the bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm remains a third-party repackaging—do not install it.

announcements.title: v2.7.4: Community Fixes Merged and Major Stability Cleanup
announcements.html:
Version 2.7.4 merges 19 community bug-fix pull requests and 8 additional local fixes, covering forwarding, channels, the workbench, and the update process. Streaming tool-call frames now include the required id/name fields and continuous indexes. Responses streams now include sequence_number. Keepalive comment frames can no longer indefinitely extend an idle timeout, and transient network failures now include error codes for proper retry handling.

Concurrent sessions no longer share a global session. Vision models with the -vl suffix are no longer incorrectly classified as text-only. Empty-string enum members in Gemini tool schemas are now removed. Channel-side fixes address the Trae cache hit rate being permanently stuck at zero, channel account tests always failing, and the model selector not refreshing after a channel model is hidden. EAC login now supports the Windows system proxy.

The workbench fixes include startup failures caused by Windows reserved port ranges and the collapse button disappearing immediately after expansion. Private files on Windows now correctly receive 0600-equivalent permissions through icacls. Installations managed by pnpm will reject in-app updates and direct users back to their original installation method. This release updates the plugin package only; the desktop application version and installers are unchanged.

New npm distribution channel: This repository now publishes the scoped package @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model, which shares the same source and version as the Release tarball. Install it with dsh plugin --profile web add @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.7.4. The bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm remains a third-party repackaging—do not install it.

announcements.title: v2.7.3: Free Lane Compatibility, Account Rotation During Queueing, and Secure Updates
announcements.html:
Version 2.7.3 updates the DSH plugin. The free lane now uses Bun transport, provides complete environment information, and migrates legacy session mappings. Reversible tool aliases have been added for the actual DSH tool set, preserving tool descriptions, parameters, and host execution capabilities. Account channels now support switching accounts within the same channel and model when an explicit queue response is received. Anonymous-slot rotation, account ownership, and authentication renewal budgets have also been fixed.

Upstream connections and concurrency slots are now released promptly when a client cancels or disconnects. Cancellation during proxy handshakes also triggers immediate cleanup. When the host cannot safely hot-reload, the updater now installs the update files and prompts the user to restart for the changes to take effect; managed installations continue to be handled by their package manager. The Chinese and English README files have also been updated with the latest community group information (group 12).

Prerequisites: The default OpenCode free inference lane requires users to install native Bun themselves; the plugin does not download it automatically. You can specify its location using OUR_FREE_MODEL_BUN. This release updates the plugin package only; the desktop application version and installers are unchanged. Compatibility fixes do not remove actual upstream quota, regional, or account restrictions.

announcements.title: v2.7.1: Completely Removed WorkBuddy Domestic/International Editions and Huawei Cloud Channels
announcements.html: Version 2.7.1 tightens channel exclusions. WorkBuddy Domestic Edition (workbuddy, also known as CodeBuddy), WorkBuddy International Edition (workbuddy-ai), Huawei Cloud MaaS (huaweicloud, including Token Plan), and Huawei Cloud CodeArts are now completely blocked from being added, logged into, or installed through the plugin marketplace in both the plugin and desktop applications. This release adds the previously missing aliases for CodeBuddy and CodeArts, along with usage notices and a disclaimer clarifying that this plugin is a personal learning project, does not provide these channels, and is not affiliated with or responsible for the use of third-party channels.

announcements.title: v2.7.0: Desktop Application Gains the Same Model Workbench
announcements.html: Version 2.7.0 brings the same Model Workbench to the desktop application. The desktop console now includes a Model Workbench page embedding the same Magpie engine as the plugin. It shares channel and account management, the model catalog, theme synchronization, and fullscreen support. Once the workbench starts, its models are merged into the aggregated model catalog and appear in the model selector alongside subscription-lane models. Channel exclusion policies for WorkBuddy and Huawei Cloud are consistent across both applications. The desktop installer now bundles the engine binary.

announcements.title: v2.6.0: Model Workbench, Subscription Lane, Native Gemini Integration; WorkBuddy and Huawei Cloud Channels Removed
announcements.html:
Version 2.6.0 updates the DSH plugin. New features include the Model Workbench (embedded engine, theme synchronization, and branding), a subscription lane (Codex/Claude/Gemini/API import and local discovery, quota queries, refresh and rotation, credentials stored locally with 0600 permissions and masked output), three intelligent routing strategies and nested routing groups, native Gemini generateContent/streamGenerateContent/countTokens endpoints, Anthropic tool_choice passthrough, and an interactive client launcher. The desktop application adds four management pages: Clients & Subscriptions, Resource Library, Routing Groups, and Aggregated Channels.

WorkBuddy and Huawei Cloud MaaS channels are not provided in this release. This exclusion applies equally to the plugin and desktop application. On first launch, a usage notice and disclaimer appear in the settings page or console; they can subsequently be accessed from the footer or sidebar. This release also fixes duplicate turn counting when a combined route passes through a subscription model and ensures the release manifest is regenerated after rebuilding from source.

announcements.title: v2.5.9: Streamlined Account Channels, Removed Legacy Resources, and Updated Community Information
announcements.html: Version 2.5.9 updates the DSH plugin. Channels that are no longer available have been removed along with their login, request-handling, UI entry points, dependencies, and documentation. The plugin retains 10 account channels, the anonymous free lane, and EAC. Desktop channel resources have been synchronized, and obsolete frontend files have been removed. Shared storage and backups remain compatible with historical formats. The README has been updated with the QR code and group number for community group 5.

announcements.title: v2.5.8: Fixed Update Retries, Qoder Thinking Levels, and Reasoning Forwarding Across Tool Rounds
announcements.html: Version 2.5.8 fixes Windows update backup-renaming retries and reuses previously verified download staging files. Qoder thinking levels are now sorted by intensity. Chat tool rounds preserve reasoning content returned by the client. The EAC DeepSeek Flash display name now includes the 1017 identifier.

announcements.title: v2.5.6: Simplified Plugin Sponsorship Cards and Unified Free Model and EAC Pages
announcements.html: Version 2.5.6 updates the DSH plugin. The free model and EAC model pages now share a compact sponsorship card at the top, with updated wording: “Get 10% cashback when you invite others.” The “Ads from Sponsors” navigation entry and detail route have been removed, while the card and its external link remain. This release also fixes an issue where hot-reload dependencies were not refreshed in certain paths, allowing old modules to continue running.

announcements.title: v2.5.5: Removed Community Group Section and Startup Sponsorship Advertisement from the Plugin
announcements.html: Version 2.5.5 updates only the DSH plugin. Community group references, group numbers, and copy buttons have been removed from the sponsorship information. The sponsorship splash advertisement that automatically appeared when the desktop plugin started has also been disabled. The sponsorship page entry point and invitation-code functionality remain available. The standalone service and desktop application shell are not updated by this release.

announcements.title: v2.5.4: Desktop Application Improvements, Plugin UI Refinements, and Advertising Updates
announcements.html:
Version 2.5.4 improves the new desktop application and plugin UI, and refines advertisement presentation.

  • The desktop application improves sponsorship entry points, light and dark themes, and narrow-window layouts.
  • The plugin adds an “Ads from Sponsors” menu with complete descriptions and supporting images available on demand.
  • Daily announcements are displayed once per local date and can be collapsed at any time. The issue preventing announcements from appearing in the host settings dialog is fixed. Pressing Esc now only collapses the announcement and returns focus to the menu.

The plugin, standalone service, and Windows desktop application are all updated to 2.5.4. Managed installations should update using a trusted tarball. Windows users should exit the old application from the system tray before installing the new version.

announcements.title: v2.5.3 Emergency Fix: Removed the EAC 60-Second No-Output Timeout
announcements.html:
Version 2.5.3 removes the EAC 60-second no-valid-output timeout introduced in 2.5.2. Queueing, silent reasoning, and waiting periods containing only heartbeat frames are no longer terminated prematurely by this rule. The legacy progressTimeoutMs setting is no longer effective. User cancellation and existing transport-disconnection detection remain unchanged.

This release does not modify OpenCode fingerprinting or admission logic. Anonymous-channel 403 / LANE_LOCKED errors must still be investigated separately from EAC waiting issues.

announcements.title: v2.5.2: Fixed Updates, Account Login, and Streaming Errors; Windows Installer Updated

link.label: View release notes and download artifacts

announcements.html:
Version 2.5.2 has been released with a plugin tarball and a complete Windows x64 installer. Fixes include GitHub API rate limits causing update failures, stale module caches, repeated announcement notifications, desktop account login problems, and incorrect request cooldowns. System prompts, blank responses, and streaming error handling have also been improved.

New features include model hiding, capability intersection display for routing chains, and an inference relay for LAN access to the standalone service. Package-manager installations should use distribution: managed and update the trusted tarball path.

Anonymous-channel upstream 403 / LANE_LOCKED errors are not claimed to be fixed. Actual availability still depends on upstream admission policies, quotas, and network conditions. EAC requests that produce no valid output for 60 seconds now fail explicitly instead of being silently retried. Please see the full release notes.

announcements.title: v2.5.1: Fixed Update Failures with a New Mirror Accessible from Mainland China; Removed org Prefix from EAC Cards
announcements.html:
Fixed failures when checking for updates. On some networks, raw.githubusercontent.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net were slow or intermittently unreachable, causing update checks to fail with no manifest source answered. This release adds a proxy mirror for update manifests and announcement subscriptions. In testing, the mirror returned identical bytes in approximately 1.3 seconds, while direct access to the original source took as long as 16 seconds and sometimes timed out.

The mirror does not retrieve files from mutable branches. Like the direct source, it first resolves the repository to a full commit SHA and then retrieves the manifest and every file using that SHA. Signature verification and per-file SHA-256 checks remain fully enabled.

The small text on EAC cards no longer displays the org/ prefix (for example, deepseek-v4.1-flash-free). The main display name remains EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free. On the server side, the external EAC channel model name has been restored to its prefixed form. The Pinned / NEW / Blast / High-Speed labels, 1M context, and thinking levels are now all effective.

Go to Settings → Plugin Updates and check for version 2.5.1.

announcements.title: v2.5.0: Fixed Free Lane 403 Errors Through Session ID Encoding Validation; EAC-design-world Added to Recommended Projects
announcements.html:
Free lane 403 errors have been fixed. Starting on 2026-10-17, the upstream service added session ID encoding validation: a 12-character hexadecimal value must represent the official client's descending timestamp (~(milliseconds << 12 | counter), with a counter from 1 to 63 and the lower 12 bits in the range 0xfc0–0xfff). Ascending values and hash digests are rejected with 403 FreeTierError.

The plugin now generates session IDs that comply with this encoding. Non-descending IDs supplied by callers are deterministically re-encoded rather than forwarded unchanged, ensuring that the same conversation continues to map to the same upstream session. Testing from the same IP showed that the original ascending ID returned 403, while the re-encoded ID returned 200.

A third project has been added to the Recommended Projects page: EAC-design-world. This is a local video production and design plugin for DeepSeek Harness, featuring multitrack editing, templates and design systems, a native preview canvas, and real file exports. Everything runs locally. If you find it useful, consider giving it a Star.

The plugin, standalone local service, and Windows desktop application shell have all been updated to 2.5.0. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to check for the update.

announcements.title: Free Lane 403 Fixed: Session ID Encoding Validation; EAC Free Models Now Use a Server-Side IP Pool
announcements.html:
The free lane is operational again. Starting on 2026-10-17, the upstream service introduced session ID encoding validation instead of checking only the ses_ format. The 12-character hexadecimal value must represent a descending timestamp (~(milliseconds << 12 | counter), with a counter from 1 to 63 and the lower 12 bits in the range 0xfc0–0xfff). Ascending values and hash digests are rejected with 403 FreeTierError.

Plugin fix: Session IDs now comply with the encoding validation rules. Non-descending IDs supplied by callers are deterministically re-encoded rather than forwarded unchanged, ensuring that the same conversation continues to map to the same upstream session. Testing from the same IP showed that the original ascending ID returned 403, while the re-encoded ID returned 200.

EAC free models now use a server-side IP pool: An anonymous-lane gateway has been deployed on the server, with outbound connections routed through a free proxy pool that automatically refreshes its list of working nodes every 30 minutes. Single-IP rate limits no longer directly affect availability. The EAC models deepseek-v4.1-flash-free and glm-5.3-flash-free have been migrated to this route. All 20 consecutive test requests succeeded.

Please upgrade the plugin before using the models.

announcements.title: Two New OpenCode Free Models Added to EAC: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free and GLM 5.3 Flash Free
announcements.html:
Two new models are now available through the EAC channel, forwarded by the OpenCode Free Lane. They appear at the top of the EAC model page with red NEW / BLAST badges and a High-Speed label:

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free (opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free)
Supports image input. Thinking levels: Off / Low / High / Maximum. The Off setting genuinely disables reasoning, reducing reasoning tokens to zero. All four levels are passed directly to the upstream provider.

GLM 5.3 Flash Free (opencode/glm-5.3-flash-free)
Native multimodal support for images, videos, and PDFs. Thinking levels: Low / High / Maximum. These settings are also passed directly to the upstream provider.

Both models are forwarded through the server-side EAC gateway with request signing and operate independently of the anonymous free lane. Before using them, complete the GitHub authorization required by the EAC channel and Star the repository.

announcements.title: v2.4.0: Free Lane Updated to OpenCode v2 Client Fingerprint; Recommended Projects Page; Fixed Aggregated Channel Entries
announcements.html:
Free lane: Updated to match the upstream v2 client introduced on 2026-10-14. The User-Agent is now opencode/latest/2.0.26/cli. Four session header mirrors have been added with identical values, and the v1-specific x-opencode-request header has been removed. The tool gate now uses the names read and shell, with definitions matching the official client exactly. tool_choice: none is no longer sent upstream. If the caller already uses either of these tool names, it is renamed with a _client suffix and restored in the response.

Recommended Projects page: A new page has been added to Settings with two project cards linking to EAC-Desktop and EAC-Pack. GitHub Stars, forks, and recent commit counts are retrieved in real time. If data cannot be retrieved, the entire section is hidden rather than displaying placeholder numbers.

Aggregated Channels: The OpenCode passwordless pool entry has been removed. It requires a per-request session fingerprint that the generic transport used by the aggregated channel cannot provide. These 10 models are already available natively through the free lane. The registry now displays 75 providers.

The plugin, standalone local service, and Windows desktop application shell have all been updated to 2.4.0. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to check for the update.

announcements.title: Recommended Projects Page Launched: EAC-Desktop, EAC-Pack, and EAC-design-world
announcements.html:
A new Recommended Projects page has been added to Settings. It features three open-source projects from the same ecosystem as this plugin. They bring agents into native desktop applications, allow hundreds of plugins to coexist, and keep video production and design workflows on your own machine. They are also part of the desktop workbench behind the EAC cooperative channel. If you find them useful, consider giving them a Star.

EAC-Desktop · Desktop Workspace
A native Tauri desktop application based on DeepSeek Harness, with a bundled Node.js runtime. Launch it with a double-click and manage project files, session changes, the plugin marketplace, and themes in one place. Installers are available for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-Desktop · Download

EAC-Pack · Plugin Integration Suite
A DSH Desktop plugin directory with batch installation and update management. It includes 72 baseline sub-plugins, theme previews, and a Prompt collection. Fixed digest manifests provide byte-for-byte verification, ensuring a complete and trustworthy installation.
github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-Pack

EAC-design-world · Design Workspace
A local video production and design plugin for DSH, featuring multitrack editing, templates and design systems, and a native preview canvas. Exports are real files, and all assets and projects remain on your own hard drive.
github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-design-world

All three projects are free, open-source, and ad-free. GitHub Stars are their only “paycheck”—each additional Star gives the developers another reason to keep building.

announcements.title: v2.3.0: Free Lane Migration and Dedicated Plugin Update Page
announcements.html:
Free lane: Requests have been migrated to the new /inference/v1 path, with session identification, tool fingerprinting, and client ownership handling completed. Session mappings are now persistent and are no longer lost when the service restarts. Upstream FreeTierError responses are explicitly identified as lane restrictions instead of misleading users into repeatedly signing in.

Plugin updates: The update functionality now has its own navigation page, centralizing version information, progress, and failure reasons. The duplicate update panel has been removed from the Settings page.

The plugin, standalone local service, and Windows desktop application shell have all been updated to 2.3.0. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to check for the update. Users of the standalone service and desktop application should install the complete updated application.

announcements.title: v2.1.0: Aggregated API for 76 Providers, Token Savings of up to 90%, Automatic Route Fallback, and Native /v1/messages
announcements.html:
Aggregated API: A new Aggregated Channels page has been added to Settings. Enter your own API key to integrate 76 providers, including NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, Gemini, DeepSeek, and local Ollama, into a unified model catalog. These models are served through the local gateway alongside the free lane. API keys are stored only in local files with 0600 permissions; the UI displays only the last four characters.

Token Savings: A new Token Savings page has been added. Tool-output compression rewrites git diff, grep, ls, build logs, and similar outputs into shorter text while preserving the same information. A 40 KB diff was measured to save 90% of its bytes. Additional features include conservative prompt modes (Concise and Ultra-Concise), five local responses that do not require an LLM call (quota checks, command prefixes, titles, suggestions, and file paths), and a cumulative savings dashboard.

Automatic Route Fallback: A new Routing page allows multiple models to be arranged into a fallback chain, such as Subscription → Low-Cost → Free. The first model that successfully produces output provides the answer. If a model encounters rate limits, refusals, or 5xx errors before delivering any content, the request automatically moves to the next model. Switching occurs before any content is delivered, so the transition is invisible within the conversation.

Local Gateway: Native Anthropic /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens endpoints have been added. Claude Code and the Anthropic SDK can connect directly without an OpenAI translation layer. The Settings page's Integration section generates configuration snippets for Claude Code, Codex, OpenAI SDK, Anthropic SDK, and curl based on the actual port and API key.

announcements.title: v2.0.0: Major Free Channel Upgrade, Kilo Lane Launch, GitHub Authorization for EAC, and Improved Login Security
announcements.html:
Free channels: Thirteen account channels have been integrated, including the new Kilo lane. Channel listings now use real logos. Each account displays its live balance and supports automatic daily check-ins. The account-pool highlights section has also been restored.

EAC cooperative channel: GitHub login and a repository Star are now required to use EAC models. Authorization is available with one click in Settings, and the browser automatically returns the authorization result to the application. Periodic Star checks have been removed from the login flow. The anonymous free lane is completely unaffected. The login process has also been strengthened: token acquisition is idempotent, gateway restarts no longer discard completed logins, and failures are reported explicitly instead of leaving the interface spinning indefinitely.

Fixes: Fixed update activation, rollback, and recovery states (#93); malicious tool calls with missing names (#92); legacy kernel fallback (#89); EAC web support (#58/#59); long conversations being blocked by the front-end WAF (#63); and long turns being cut off when the account pool is saturated (#69/#70). EAC authorization is now mandatory: users who have not signed in with GitHub and starred the repository can no longer use EAC. After upgrading, complete GitHub authorization in Settings.

announcements.title: v1.5.0: GitHub Authorization Required for EAC (Login + Star); Free Lane Unaffected
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.5.0 introduces a per-user authorization gate for the EAC cooperative channel: sign in with GitHub and Star the repository to use EAC models.

  • Why — EAC is a cooperative channel whose capacity scales with the number of repository Stars (each Star adds 1.5 account-pool capacity units). Linking access to Stars helps align the people using the service with those supporting its capacity.
  • How to use it — Go to Settings → Our Free Model → EAC Channel Authorization → “Sign in with GitHub.” Your browser opens the authorization page automatically. Sign in and Star the repository, then return to the application. No copying or pasting is required. The plugin automatically completes token acquisition. If you have not starred the repository, the authorization page provides an “I've starred it, check again” option, so you do not need to sign in again.
  • Removing your Star revokes access — The server checks repository Stars every 12 hours. If you remove your Star, authorization becomes invalid within the next verification window. GitHub outages and rate limits preserve existing authorization rather than incorrectly revoking it.
  • The free lane is completely unaffected — Models in the OpenCode lane do not pass through the server and continue working without login or a Star.
  • Transition period — This release initially operates in compatibility mode, meaning EAC remains available without login. A separate announcement will be published before enforcement becomes mandatory. We recommend authorizing in advance to avoid service interruptions.
  • Privacy — Only the minimum read:user permission is requested, solely for Star verification. Authorization data is stored only on your machine and the server. You can sign out at any time from Settings, which immediately revokes authorization on the server.

All offline bundles, including the newly added authorization-gate bundle, have passed verification. The manifests have been re-signed byte for byte. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.4.7: Extended Time Limits for Long Responses; Normal Extended Reasoning Is No Longer Cut Off When the Account Pool Is Saturated
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.7 fixes the issue reported in #69/#70: long reasoning sessions were being terminated by STREAM_CUT after exactly eight minutes.

  • Overall turn timeout increased from 480 to 900 seconds; recovery timeout increased from 180 to 300 seconds. Previously, the eight-minute wall-clock limit consistently terminated normal long-running responses when the account pool was saturated. In observed cases, the pool had a capacity of 1923 and 2451 concurrent requests, first-token latency ranged from 34 to 220 seconds, and deep reasoning exceeded six minutes. One example displayed “Deep reasoning in progress, elapsed time 6 minutes 16 seconds” before reporting reached its 480s time limit. The new limits allow these responses to complete normally.
  • Protection against hung requests remains unchanged. The transport layer still has a separate 300-second idle timeout for periods with absolutely no incoming bytes, reset whenever a data chunk arrives. The wall-clock timeout only serves as a safeguard for responses that continuously produce frames but progress very slowly. Values can still only be reduced, and each turn remains limited to a maximum of two physical requests.

Actual long-response speed still depends on queueing in the shared upstream account pool. Lower thinking levels can significantly reduce waiting time. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.4.6: EAC Cooperative Channel Opens to Web Clients (#58/#59); Long Conversations No Longer Blocked by the Front-End WAF (#63); Improved Error Classification
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.6 addresses several issues tracked in the project's issue list:

  • EAC cooperative channel now supports web clients (#58/#59/#61) — The host admission gate now recognizes web profiles declared by the kernel (web / web-desktop). The Deepseek Harness EAC desktop shell using the web-desktop profile and the dsh web combination can now access all six EAC models. Channel credential sealing and signing remain unchanged. Hosts that cannot be identified still keep EAC hidden, but the model list in Settings now displays a clear explanation instead of silently omitting the models (#60).
  • Long conversations are no longer blocked by the front-end WAF (#63) — The server-side front-end WAF now includes /eac/v1/ in its URL allowlist. Previously, request bodies exceeding 200,000 characters were blocked by a “Nginx buffer overflow” page. During peak periods, this happened 370 times per day. Such requests now reach the signed gateway directly. The plugin also improves error handling: HTML error pages returned by front-end proxies (WAF/CDN) are reduced to a readable one-line message identifying the actual cause. WAF 403 pages are no longer incorrectly diagnosed as invalid credentials, preventing unnecessary repeated logins. HTML responses received with HTTP 200 are now treated as non-retryable, preventing the same oversized request from being automatically sent three times.
  • First-token latency findings and an additional fix (#66) — Tests and server logs confirm that the signing lane, SSE keepalive, and concurrency gate all function correctly. The 34–221 second first-token delay originates from queueing in the relay's shared upstream account pool. The upstream pool contains approximately 800 channels, with an average response time of 32.5 seconds and some slow channels exceeding two minutes. The plugin now forwards thinking frames correctly, ensuring that reasoning content is not lost once a slow channel begins producing frames. To reduce the waiting time itself, use a lower thinking level.
  • Update trust-chain improvements (#64) — The 1.4.5 manifest had four files that differed by one byte following a repository rename commit, causing all one-click updates from older versions to fail. This was corrected when the 1.4.5 manifest was re-signed. This release also passed manifest consistency checks and full end-to-end update tests using the actual release manifest.

All offline bundles have passed testing and the manifest has been re-signed byte for byte. The WAF allowlist change was verified using real signed requests: both 64 KB and 300 KB request bodies reached the gateway successfully, without affecting other websites on the same machine. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.4.5: Outbound Proxy Support (Subscription/Single Proxy), Hardened EAC Signing Lane, Automatic Continuation After Truncation, and Settings Subpath Fix
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.5 combines several maintenance improvements. Users affected by regional restrictions and unstable network routes now have access to outbound proxy support, alongside fixes for several frequently reported issues.

  • Outbound proxy (subscription / single proxy) — Upstream requests from the plugin can now use your own outbound connection: either an airport subscription (automatically starts local mihomo, tests nodes, selects the fastest node, and removes nodes returning 429) or a single HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy. The Settings page displays the current best node and connection latency. Subscription URLs are treated as credentials and are read only when you explicitly click Show. Updates, announcements, and the EAC lane do not use this proxy, keeping their failure domains isolated.
  • Hardened EAC signing lane — Signed request bodies are now transmitted directly through Node's core http(s) modules. Local plugins that modify fetch, such as billion-context, can no longer access or modify the signed bytes. Previously, the gateway's “request signature rejected” error could be incorrectly diagnosed as invalid credentials. The new implementation explicitly identifies local proxy modifications (#50).
  • Fixed backend connectivity when the Settings page is deployed under a subpath — Reverse-proxy deployments no longer lose their path prefixes. Compatibility for dsh-app:// relay requests on desktop has also been merged from a community PR. Admission errors now return 503 with structured diagnostic logs (#49/#54).
  • Automatic continuation after truncation — When an answer reaches the output limit and is truncated, the plugin feeds the already-generated text back to the model and automatically continues once. You no longer need to manually send “Continue” (#28).
  • Dashboard — Added an account-pool load dashboard displaying capacity, 24-hour activity, and current concurrency. The gateway process determines whether the pool is healthy, busy, or overloaded in real time. A one-line summary of the most recent turn has also been added (#26).
  • Default per-IP gateway concurrency reduced from 20 to 5 — An LLM streaming request occupies an upstream connection for tens of seconds to several minutes. The previous default allowed a single user to saturate the shared lane and overload the entire server. This was one of the issues observed in #55.

All offline bundles have passed testing and the manifest has been re-signed byte for byte. Local gateway and real-machine self-tests covering conversations, tools, vision, and updates all passed. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.4.4: Removed Leaked DeepSeek DSML Control Markers; <｜DSML｜ calls> No Longer Appears After Reasoning
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.4 fixes a display issue affecting some DeepSeek V4 models. At the moment when a model finishes reasoning and prepares to call a tool, it could accidentally expose the internal control marker <｜DSML｜ calls> as visible response text because the server-side sampling process did not intercept that special token.

  • Streaming marker removal — The plugin's stream parser now removes visible <｜DSML｜...> control fragments in real time. Partial markers are buffered until they can be identified, preventing incomplete fragments from leaking into the output. Actual tool-call frames are unaffected, and tools continue to execute normally.
  • Both lanes are covered — The anonymous free lane and EAC channel use the same parser. All six DeepSeek/Kimi/GLM models in the EAC channel are also protected.
  • The three-attempt download retry introduced in version 1.4.3 remains unchanged.

All 21 offline bundles passed testing, and the manifest was re-signed byte for byte using Ed25519. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.4.3: Three Per-File Download Attempts During Updates; Temporary Connection Drops No Longer Fail the Entire Package
announcements.html: Our Free Model v1.4.3 fixes the update mechanism itself: each file is now downloaded with up to three attempts. A user upgrading from 1.3.1 to 1.4.2 encountered staging failed: …: fetch failed. Connections from mainland China to CDN endpoints can temporarily fluctuate, and previously each file had only one download attempt. A brief interruption could therefore fail the entire package. Now, transport failures (connection drops, timeouts, 5xx, and 429 responses) trigger automatic backoff and two additional attempts. Integrity failures, including size or SHA-256 mismatches, are still rejected immediately. These failures indicate a trust-chain violation and must never be treated as recoverable network errors. All 21 offline bundles passed testing, and the manifest was re-signed byte for byte using Ed25519. If an update fails, simply click “Update Now” again. Starting with 1.4.3, the updater automatically handles temporary network interruptions.

announcements.title: v1.4.2: EAC Cooperative Channel Launched with Six Flagship Models, 1M Context, and Vision; Signed Gateway, Seven Security Gates, Thinking Levels, and Eight Merged Contributor PRs
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.2 brings together all development since the September release: a new EAC cooperative channel, its signed gateway and anti-abuse gates, and eight contributor pull requests.

  • EAC cooperative channel (desktop-only) — Six flagship models are now available: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1M context, vision, thinking Off/Low/High/Extreme, 384K output), Kimi K3 (1M context, vision, advanced reasoning, Agentic), Kimi K2.6 (262K context, vision), GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3 Flash (1M context, deep reasoning), and GPT-OSS 20B (open weights). Channel credentials are sealed into three fragments using AES-256-GCM, with keys derived at runtime through HKDF. The host admission gate verifies that the application is running on desktop before unlocking the models. The EAC model count remains zero in the web profile. If the gate is locked, the request fails once with LANE_LOCKED instead of triggering repeated retries.
  • Signed gateway: real API keys never leave the server — The actual upstream key exists only in the gateway environment. Plugin requests carry HMAC-SHA256 signatures, with a replay window of ±600 seconds, constant-time comparison, support for multiple keys during rotation, and only two permitted routes. SSE pre-flushing: Once signature verification succeeds, the gateway immediately returns HTTP 200, streaming headers, and keepalive heartbeats. This prevents inference models with first-token delays of 20–140 seconds from being terminated by Nginx's 60-second or Cloudflare's 100-second limits. A 124-second GLM-5.3 response was successfully completed in testing. Upstream rejections are returned as in-stream error frames, preserving existing error classification.
  • Seven anti-abuse gates verified in real tests — Requests without signatures, forged signatures, and replayed requests return 401; requests outside the allowlist return 403; payloads exceeding 8 MB return 413; unknown routes return 404; and 61 requests per minute return 429. Each gate was verified with real requests. Additional protection includes 20 concurrent requests per IP, model allowlists, and Cloudflare edge protection. The gateway dashboard tracks usage using salted IP hashes, and the New API dashboard automatically adds an EAC Dashboard entry to its sidebar.
  • Thinking controls — Thinking-level menus follow the model declarations used by ZCode: DeepSeek (Off/Low/High/Extreme), Kimi (Low/High/Extreme), GLM (Low/High/Extreme), and GPT-OSS (Low/Medium/High). The default level must be one of the options available for its model. EAC requests include system prompts to prevent excessive reasoning, with automatic continuation as a fallback for silent turns.
  • Contributor pull requests merged — #23/#24/#25/#27/#35/#36/#37/#38/#39, covering LAN relay forwarding, synchronization of simultaneous startup operations, port-increment notifications, and continuation handling for refusal/pause_turn.
  • Usability improvements — HTML error pages from front-end proxies are reduced to readable one-line messages. The free-lane rate-limit badge now says “Temporarily Unavailable” because fluctuations in this public upstream pool do not indicate that the user's own quota has been exhausted.

All 21 offline bundles passed testing, and the manifest was re-signed byte for byte using Ed25519. The EAC channel is visible only in the DSH desktop application. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.3.2: Signed Update Trust Chain (#19); Fixed Tool Calls Through Forwarding Ports (#20/#21); Quota Backoff (#13); Improved Heatmap Layout (#11)
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.3.2 addresses five issues from the project's issue tracker:

  • Replaced the root of trust for the update mechanism (#19) — Previously, the update manifest was plain JSON downloaded over HTTPS. File hashes were stored inside the manifest itself, meaning anyone who could forge the manifest could also forge its hashes. This also placed the third-party jsDelivr CDN inside the trust chain. Now every manifest must carry an Ed25519 signature created with the release private key, while the public key is pinned inside the plugin. The private key is never stored in the repository. Compromising a mirror, including jsDelivr, can now only cause an update to fail; it can no longer lead to arbitrary code execution. The feedUrl setting is completely separated from update sources and now only redirects announcements. Manifest base values are restricted to relative paths. Plugin API request bodies are limited to 1 MB. Forwarding listeners now bind according to DNS resolution and require loopback addresses, preventing a hosts-file entry that redirects localhost to a routable interface from bypassing quota restrictions.
  • Fixed tool calls through forwarding ports (#20/#21) — Previously, streaming tool_calls[].index values shared a counter with reasoning blocks. The first tool call could therefore arrive with index 2 or higher, creating gaps in arrays assembled by index-based clients and causing parameters to be merged incorrectly. Tool-call indexes are now independently renumbered starting from zero. If a model calls injected decoy tools such as bash, read, or grep that were added to pass upstream fingerprint checks, those calls are now suppressed in the forwarding layer instead of being passed to clients that never registered them. Streaming responses also correctly return length when tool-call arguments are truncated by the output limit. /v1/responses now supports instructions, max_output_tokens, and streaming, and its streaming output indexes no longer collide.
  • Improved quota-limit handling (#13) — The lane's 429 responses include an increasing retry-after value. The plugin previously retried twice automatically, turning one rate-limit response into three requests against the same restriction. It now reports 429 immediately. After an entire availability-probe round returns 429, probes use exponential backoff from 30 to 120 minutes. Manual probes, outbound-route changes, and startup probes are exempt. Availability checks no longer compete with actual conversations for the same per-IP quota pool. The speed-test button now uses the default thinking level and a more generous frontend timeout, preventing near-certain failures that would otherwise waste quota.
  • Improved heatmap layout (#11) — Cell gaps have been removed and corner radii reduced, creating a continuous appearance similar to the GitHub contribution graph.
  • Other improvements — Route-specific frontend timeouts have been increased (240 seconds for speed tests and 600 seconds for updates). Announcement subscriptions now reconnect with exponential backoff from 30 seconds to 5 minutes after disconnection instead of remaining permanently inactive. Successful updates clear old error banners, and failed store persistence now generates a diagnostic log entry.

All 20 offline bundles and tsc --noEmit passed. Installation and update workflows were also verified in a real DSH host environment. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.3.1: Tool Results Finally Reach the Model (#9); Interrupted Long Reasoning No Longer Reported as Success (#10); Upstream Sources Documented in README (#8)
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.3.1 addresses three issues from the project's issue tracker:

  • Tool calls and results were not being delivered to the model (#9) — DSH used two different message formats across two kernel generations to represent tool results. Before V4, results were stored in user messages containing tool-result content blocks. Starting with V4, they were represented as role:'tool' messages. The plugin recognized only the latter format. Consequently, every agent task using the free lane on kernel versions DSH 0.1.5 / AIO 6.9.3 failed to send tool results back to the model. The model repeatedly issued the same tool call and continued claiming that image reading had returned no content until the user manually stopped it. Both formats are now recognized and projected into the three-line format. Images embedded in tool results are no longer discarded. An additional fix addresses injected bash decoy tools that models actually attempted to call, resulting in up to 24 unknown-tool errors in a single session. The plugin now promotes the kernel's real shell tool (called pwsh in this generation on Windows) to the bash alias and restores the original tool name when the result is returned, making the call executable.
  • Streams closed prematurely by upstream were incorrectly reported as successful (#10) — When the gateway closed an SSE stream without sending either a finish token or a usage frame, the plugin previously fell back to stop. As a result, a response that spent five minutes reasoning and then went silent could be marked as completed, with statistics showing ok:true / 0 tokens. This is now treated as an immediate failure. The interface displays “This turn failed” and the exact number of seconds before truncation. Statistics retain truncated and noUsage for auditing. Retries are now limited to truncations where not a single token has been generated. Testing in a real dsh web session showed that this lane consistently terminated pure reasoning turns after 304 seconds. The previous implementation retried the same five-minute response twice more, producing three identical failures over 15 minutes, with llm/retry events at 304 and 608 seconds and turn/end at 912 seconds. Since the limit originated from the length of the turn rather than a transient network problem, retrying could not solve it.
  • Upstream sources documented in README (#8) — A new section lists the upstream sources. There is only one: OpenCode's Zen gateway (https://opencode.ai), using its publicly available passwordless quota without any third-party relay or account pool. All four categories of outbound destinations are explicitly listed.

These changes were cross-verified against real session records from both DSH kernel versions 0.1.5 and 0.1.7. Go to Settings → Plugin Updates to upgrade with one click.

announcements.title: v1.3.0: Added Managed Installation Mode for Ecosystem Bundles; Fixed Duplicate Forwarding-Port Restarts
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.3.0 prepares the project for integration into the EAC ecosystem:

  • Managed installation mode (distribution=managed) — When the plugin is managed by an integration bundle or package manager, in-app updates, announcement sources, and hot reloading are disabled (the corresponding APIs return 409). Release files and update timing are controlled by the package manager. The Settings API cannot reverse managed mode. Users who install the plugin independently are completely unaffected.
  • Upstream kernel dependencies consolidated under adapter/ — The only location in the entire package allowed to import @deepseek-ai/* is adapter/kernel.js. All other modules must use the defined compatibility layer, with automated tests enforcing this boundary to prevent upstream dependencies from spreading again.
  • Fixed duplicate forwarding-port restarts — Previously, every save operation on the Settings page restarted an already-running local forwarding service, even when its host and port already matched the requested configuration. This invalidated Bearer tokens copied by clients. The service is now reused whenever the desired configuration is already satisfied.
  • Directory and integrity records — Added a manifest 0.15 directory entry (catalog/dsh-plugin.json), provenance records, and integrity manifests. All SHA-256 values are generated by the build script from the actual bytes after LF normalization. No placeholder or fabricated values are used.

Users with independent installations can upgrade with one click from Settings → Plugin Updates. Updates for managed installations are scheduled by their integration bundle.

announcements.title: v1.2.2: Fixed One-Click Updates; Increased Thinking Budgets by Model; Unavailable Models Removed from the Selector
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.2.2 addresses the issues reported in the project's issue tracker:

  • In-app updates are working again (#1) — The release manifest in version 1.2.1 did not match the actual files. As a result, one-click updates from every older version failed during verification. The manifest has been regenerated, and a new build-manifest.mjs --check command now exits with a non-zero status whenever the manifest and actual files do not match. It has been integrated into npm test and CI.
  • Models that cannot disable reasoning are no longer prematurely truncated (#2) — Models such as MiMo V2.6 use the same budget for reasoning and final output. Their three overall limits have therefore been increased to 4,096 / 16,384 / the model's maximum. Descriptions on each model card and thinking-level option are now generated from the actual values sent to the model, eliminating discrepancies such as the interface displaying 8K while the request actually sends 16K.
  • Models identified as unavailable are no longer included in the selector (#3) — A model is removed from the dropdown only when the gateway explicitly identifies that its ID is not routable. The rejection reason remains visible in Settings. 5xx errors, rate limits, timeouts, and network failures are no longer treated as definitive judgments about a model. On fresh installations, models that have not yet completed availability checks remain selectable.
  • Composition can now be installed without a browser UI (#4) — The plugin treats the model lane as its only hard dependency. The Settings interface runs independently on its own fiber and waits for the web service to become available before mounting. This allows model inference to work even in environments without a web server. (A real-world DSH TUI environment has not yet been tested.)
  • Streaming responses are identified by their body rather than their headers (#6) — Under heavy gateway load, the gateway may return a complete set of SSE frames with an application/json content type. The plugin now identifies the response based on the actual body structure. Previously inspected bytes are fed back into the stream, preventing the entire turn from failing and avoiding incorrect classification of otherwise usable models as unavailable.

Users on older versions can upgrade with one click from Settings → Plugin Updates. New installations require no action. (Feature request #5, polling multiple outbound nodes, is outside the scope of this release.)
